samples.summary: The canonical rendering doc is now contradicted; the new `keepDirty` exception is documented in the collaboration doc instead
samples.evidence: `docs/design/docs/docs-rendering-optimization.md` is the canonical subsystem doc for `recomputeLayout` / `dirtyBlockIds`. It states the invariant twice: line 197 `dirtyBlockIds = undefined; // reset after layout`, and line 246 "Race between dirty tracking and render | dirtyBlockIds is reset synchronously inside recomputeLayout". This change adds `recomputeLayout({ keepDirty })` in `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts`, which deliberately does NOT reset the set (restoring `undefined` as an empty set), and documents that rule at length in `docs/design/docs/docs-collaboration.md` instead. Per CONTRIBUTING's "fold into the canonical subsystem doc" discipline, the rendering-optimization doc should carry the exception to its own invariant; as written it is now stale and a reader of the rendering doc will believe the reset is unconditional. Note the nested-doc link/consistency lane does not recurse into `docs/design/docs/`, so nothing mechanical catches this.

samples.summary: The undo-unit rule is now written three times (EditorAPI / TextEditor / text-box-editor) instead of once
samples.evidence: The design doc added by this change says it outright: "`indent` / `outdent` / `toggleList` exist three times — `editor.ts`'s `EditorAPI`, `TextEditor`, and `text-box-editor.ts` — with the same `MAX_LIST_LEVEL` and `INDENT_STEP`, so the batching shape is now written in each rather than once, and a future change to the undo-unit rule has to be made three times." The change adds a fourth invariant (the `doc.batch(...)` wrapper plus the "snapshot outside the batch" ordering) to each of the three copies — `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts` (indent/outdent/toggleList), `packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts` (handleIndent/handleOutdent/handleTab), `packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts` (toggleList/indent/outdent). This repo expects reuse (Slides reuses the Docs engine; shared code in `@wafflebase/core`). The deferral to issue #1048 with a stated reason (the EditorAPI copy is selection-scoped, the TextEditor one caret-scoped, and `textEditor` is absent on a read-only mount) is a reasonable call, so this is tidiness rather than a behavioral cost — but the divergence risk is now larger than before the change.

samples.summary: `DocStore.applyStyles` already existed as the "many style writes, one undo unit" primitive; batching adds a second overlapping mechanism and leaves its contract doc stale
samples.evidence: `packages/docs/src/store/store.ts:123-126` documents `applyStyles` precisely as the fix for this class of problem: "a loop of `applyStyle()` calls produces one undo unit per call on stores (like `YorkieDocStore`) whose undo granularity is tied to the write itself." `Doc.dropStaleStyleOffAll` and `stepSelectionFontSize` both use it. The new code instead wraps `doc.applyInlineStyle` / `applyInlineStyleToCells` in `doc.batch()` at `view/editor.ts` (`applyStyleImpl`, `insertLink`) and `view/text-editor.ts` (`applyStyleToSelection`). Two primitives now answer the same question, and `applyStyles`'s interface comment — the only place the rule is stated on the interface — is now only true outside a batch. Either routing the slice writes through `applyStyles`, or a note on the interface that `batch()` is the general mechanism and `applyStyles` the specialized one, would keep one answer.

samples.summary: The superseded `GET /share-links/:token/resolve` is retained with zero in-repo callers and no removal tracking
samples.evidence: `resolveShareLink` (the only caller in the repo — grep for `resolveShareLink` across `packages/frontend/src` returns `api/share-links.ts`, `api/url.test.ts` and `app/shared/shared-document.tsx` only) now POSTs. The GET route is justified in both the controller comment and `docs/design/sharing.md` as "kept for one-shot callers that already exist (an older frontend served during a rollout)", which is a sound transitional argument — but nothing records when it goes away. The result is two permanently-documented public ways to resolve the same token, one of which the same doc argues leaks the credential into third-party access logs. A follow-up issue reference (as was done for #1048 on the triplication) would close this.

samples.summary: `MUTATING_METHODS` — the deny-list this repo's own code documents as the "fails open" anti-pattern behind #989 — is now load-bearing for a second condition (disposal)
samples.evidence: `packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts:6-19` argues at length that a list of mutators to deny "fails open: the new write forwards, and the gate still reads as complete. That is exactly how `MUTATING_METHODS` in `view/editor.ts` came to be missing `getStore`/`getDoc` in the first place (issue #989)." This change hoists that same list into `neuterMutations()` and makes it the gate for disposal as well as read-only — doubling what a forgotten entry costs, with only the comment "Keep in sync when adding a mutating method" enforcing it. The blast radius is genuinely reduced (mutators that write through `doc` / `pageSetupGuardedStore` are also stopped by `revocableStore`), but the api members that write via the raw `docStore` — `setDocStyles`, `updateStyleToMatch`, `resetNamedStyle`, `resetAllNamedStyles` through `withNamedStyleChange` — have only this list guarding them. Inverting the list to an allowlist of non-mutating `EditorAPI` members, the way `read-only.ts` did for `DocStore`, is the shape the repo already chose.

samples.summary: Three independent efforts are bundled in one change: #1045 undo batching, share-link live revalidation (incl. a new backend endpoint), and editor disposal/revocation
samples.evidence: The diff's own comments attribute the batching work to issue #1045 and the revocation/revalidation work to a share-link `editor` → `viewer` downgrade — different subsystems, different design docs (`docs/design/docs/docs-collaboration.md` vs `docs/design/sharing.md`), a new public backend route, and a `useState`/`useEffect` → react-query rewrite of `SharedDocumentByToken`. No stated Non-Goal is crossed (I checked `Goals / Non-Goals` in both docs), and each piece is individually documented, so this costs review surface rather than correctness. Flagged so it can be weighed: a reviewer cannot accept the undo fix without also accepting a new polling architecture and a new API endpoint.

samples.summary: Unauthenticated 60 s poll per open tab with `staleTime: 0` and no server-side caching or rate-limit consideration recorded
samples.evidence: `refetchInterval: SHARE_LINK_REVALIDATE_MS` (60 s) plus `refetchOnWindowFocus: true` and `staleTime: 0` means every open shared tab issues an unauthenticated DB-backed lookup every minute, and a refetch on every focus and remount on top. `docs/design/sharing.md` acknowledges the volume ("one unauthenticated lookup per minute per open tab") but records no caching, throttling or rate-limiting consideration for a public, token-guessable endpoint. Worth one sentence in the design doc on why that load is acceptable, or a backoff when the tab is idle.
